final_label: GO step after a rewarded visit to S1 (or unknown previous state) when belief does not favor S2

with_model_outputs.label: GO step after a rewarded trial when the agent chooses a1
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at GO (never at D1 or D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward == 1; zero activity after unrewarded trials), and almost only when the agent is about to choose a1 (99% of mass). The action is the agent own upcoming choice, which it computes; the observed-only equivalent using the policy, (phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & (choice > 2), scores about the same on dev (F1 0.947), as does model_act == 1. So this is a rewarded-and-choosing-a1 feature, not a future-outcome feature. Previous action and hidden good state are weaker (F1 0.78 / 0.84). Magnitude is high and near-saturated for confident a1 choices (choice logit > 8 has 74% rate); the weak lowest-quartile activations are rewarded GO steps where the agent picks a2 or has a less confident a1 preference. It does not fire on unrewarded trials, on D1/D2, or on most a2 choices.

issues: The checkable claims hold: the feature is active only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps), never after an unrewarded trial (prev_reward==0: 0 of 401340 active), action==1 carries 99% of the mass, and the original predicate's dev F1 is 0.947. Policy-only versions (choice>2, model_act==1) do score about the same (dev F1 0.947).

There is a systematic false-positive class the explanation misses. The feature stays off when the previous reward came at S2, even if the agent now picks a1. For (phase==GO)&(prev_reward==1)&(action==1)&(prev_state==2), precision is 0.010 on 6357 dev steps. These are mostly trials where a1 had a rare transition to S2 that paid off and the agent repeated a1. The test-split misses output shows them again (rel +1 windows like '[+0] r1 a1 S2R | [+1] r1 a1'). The same subset with prev_state==1 has precision 0.999.

The same variable explains the misses. After a reward at S1, the feature also fires on many GO steps where the agent ends up choosing a2: (GO)&(prev_reward==1)&(action==2)&(prev_state==1) is active 37.6% of the time. What matters is the previous rewarded state, combined with the a1 choice logit not being strongly negative. It is not the action itself.

The explanation says prev_action predicates score worse (0.78). That is true alone, but it hides the fact that prev_state is a necessary conjunct. The label 'rewarded trial, choosing a1' overclaims: in this data the feature means 'rewarded at S1, and not strongly preferring a2'.

The window's first trial (rel -3) has prev_state -1 (unknown inside the window), which is why the feature's activity looks less dependent on prev_state there. The improved predicate treats unknown as allowed (prev_state != 2).
skeptic.revised_label: GO step after a trial rewarded at S1, unless the agent strongly prefers a2 (observed-only)

with_model_outputs.final_label: GO step after a trial rewarded at S1, unless the agent strongly prefers a2 (observed-only)

label: GO step after a rewarded visit to S1 (or unknown previous state) when belief does not favor S2
explanation: Fires only at GO steps, only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew at D1 was 1), and almost only when that reward came from S1 (prev_state 1; prev_state -1 at window starts). Requiring the ideal-observer belief P(S1 good) > 0.4 removes most false positives, which are rewarded-S2 histories or window-start trials where the history favors S2. Remaining false positives are mostly window-start GO steps where the earlier history is thin. Without the belief term, prev_reward==1 & prev_state!=2 gives dev F1 0.86 (recall 1.0, precision 0.76). Magnitude not analyzed.

issues: Claims check out: GO-only, zero activity after unrewarded trials, essentially zero after rewarded S2 (precision 0.0006), rewarded-S1 branch precision 0.99, belief<=0.4 after rewarded S1 precision 0.19 (so the belief cut is justified).

Remaining FPs are concentrated, as stated, on window-start GO (prev_state == -1: precision 0.80, vs 0.97 with choice>0). A stricter belief cut there (0.5) only moves test F1 0.958 -> 0.960, so it is an observability limit, not a missing rule.
Model output adds little (choice>0 added: test F1 0.965 vs 0.958).
